Team Trump privately admits it's illegal. They're doing it anyway, largely
because the president of the United States got [mad at his TV
again](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-love-me-ads-pathetic-reason).

Over the past week, Donald Trump and his White House have rolled out a series
of campaign-style TV ads - paid for by the U.S. taxpayer and federal
government - imploring viewers to, among other things, **" Love Me"** and
reject the **" communists"** and **" warmongers,"** in a **" final battle."
**(Several Trump advisers concede to **Zeteo** that it verges on self-satire
that this president [would run ](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-iran-war-doomed-
from-start)_[against](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-iran-war-doomed-from-start)_[
warmongering at this point](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-iran-war-doomed-from-
start).)

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

One of the ads is virtually identical to a 2024 Trump campaign ad, as if to
collapse any notion that these ads aren't geared toward the fast-approaching
2026 elections or openly partisan politics. While federal laws very clearly
prohibit government use of taxpayer dollars to fund purely political
propaganda campaigns, the second Trump administration has exhibited a profound
commitment to its unique legal philosophy: **"**_**[What are you gonna do
about it?](https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-features/trump-
strategy-federal-freeze-buyout-inspector-general-1235250857/)**_**"**

Spokespeople for the White House have insisted there's nothing illegal about
their ad campaign, claiming that the taxpayer-funded TV spots are **" public
service announcements"** and not partisan propaganda meant to influence the
2026 midterms.

This claim is somewhat undermined by the fact that President Trump himself,
according to two sources with knowledge of the matter, has privately referred
to them as **" midterm ads."**
